hook.line: A complaint letter lives on one fact: something that should work does not. The oven at the café dies the day before Vale's big order, and Tomás needs the exact phrase.
hook.es: El horno está fuera de servicio desde ayer.
hook.en: The oven has been out of service since yesterday.

examples.es: El ascensor está fuera de servicio desde el lunes.
examples.en: The elevator has been out of service since Monday.

examples.es: Este baño está fuera de uso.
examples.en: This restroom is out of use.

examples.es: La máquina de café está fuera de servicio.
examples.en: The coffee machine is out of order.

examples.es: El teléfono estuvo fuera de servicio todo el día.
examples.en: The phone was out of service all day.

rule:
*Está fuera de servicio* says something is out of order. It suggests it used to work and should work again. A close cousin is *fuera de uso* (not to be used).

In everyday Colombian Spanish, *dañado* is the word for broken: *El cajero está dañado*. To say it broke, use *se dañó*: *El horno se dañó ayer*.

For "since" plus a time, use *desde*: *desde el lunes*. English says "has been out of order since". Spanish uses the plain present: *está… desde el lunes*.
smallPrint: Teachers call the *se* in *se dañó* an accidental *se*: the thing broke by itself and nobody is blamed.

options: The ATM is new.
The ATM broke yesterday.

The oven was repaired yesterday.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *El ascensor ___ fuera de servicio desde el lunes.* (*está* or *es*) The elevator has been out of service since Monday.
yourTurn.answer: El ascensor está fuera de servicio desde el lunes.
yourTurn.why: Being out of order is a condition, so it takes *está*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *El horno ___ ayer.* (*está dañado* or *se dañó*) The oven broke down yesterday.
yourTurn.why: *Ayer* points to the moment it broke, so *se dañó*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: This restroom is out of use.
yourTurn.answer: Este baño está fuera de uso.
yourTurn.why: *Fuera de uso* says nobody should use it.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The coffee machine is out of order.
yourTurn.answer: La máquina de café está fuera de servicio.
yourTurn.why: *Está fuera de servicio* is the standard phrase for out of order.
*Dañado* is the everyday word for broken.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural: *El cajero está dañado.*
yourTurn.why: The article, the noun, the verb and *dañado* all go plural.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *El ascensor está fuera de servicio.*
yourTurn.answer: El ascensor no está fuera de servicio.

pitfalls.wrong: El ascensor es fuera de servicio.
pitfalls.right: El ascensor está fuera de servicio.
pitfalls.why: Out of order is a state that can change, so *está*.

pitfalls.wrong: El ascensor está fuera de servicio por el lunes.
pitfalls.right: El ascensor está fuera de servicio desde el lunes.
pitfalls.why: For "since" plus a time, Spanish uses *desde*, not *por*.
Without *se* it sounds like the oven damaged something else.

personal: Think of something broken near you right now and say it: *… está fuera de servicio* or *… está dañado*.
